descriptions: The supreme truth from which the world's birth, maintenance and end proceed, self-luminous, free of deception (BhP 1.1.1).
One non-dual reality called Brahman, Paramātman and Bhagavān (BhP 1.2.11); Bhagavān has the six excellences (VP 6.5.74-79).
The world is the śakti of the supreme Brahman, like the spreading light of a fire (VP 1.22.56); Viṣṇu's śakti is threefold (VP 6.7.61).
One Lord takes the names Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva by function (VP 1.2.66).
Śiva alone is both partless Brahman and with form, worshipped in the liṅga (ŚiP 1.5.10-13); the unmarked is the root of the mark (LiP 1.3.1).
The Goddess is eternal, the world is her form; she alone exists and her powers return into her (DM 1; 10).
negations: the Lord's gross and subtle forms negated as superimposed by ignorance, for the vision of Brahman (BhP 1.3.30-33)
the supreme reality cannot be spoken, beyond words (VP 6.7.100)
Brahman beyond sat and asat before creation (BhP 2.9.32)
relation_to_self: Varies by text: non-difference once ignorance is gone (VP 6.7.93-96; BhP 12.5.11) alongside the devotee's eternal service that refuses even oneness (BhP 3.29.13); the self is 'made of nirvāṇa and knowledge' (VP 6.7.22).
relation_to_world: The world is the Lord's power and play (līlā), manifested and withdrawn in cycles of creation and dissolution; the Lord pervades beings as the elements pervade things, 'in them and not in them' (BhP 2.9.34).
caveat: The Purāṇas are not one school: Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva and Śākta Purāṇas each name their deity as the ultimate and often subordinate the others; passages of identity (VP 1.2.66; the Kūrma) coexist with sectarian ranking. Commentators read the same Purāṇa as non-dual (Śrīdhara) or as teaching eternal difference (Madhva) or inconceivable difference-in-identity (Jīva). A 'one truth' reading is supported by some passages and rejected by sectarian commentators.
